metadata.description: Unique Object Identifier. This is the "oid" that is returned by queries on the Objects Table. This ID can be used to retrieve additional metadata for an Object or lightcurve.
Filter for the lightcurve photometry: 1 => g; 2 => r; 3 => i.
The survey Field Identifier. Lightcurves in DR24 are spread across 1,286 fields. This identifier can be used to retrieve additional archive metadata.

The readout-channel Identifier (or CCD-Quadrant index) that contains the object. The rcid runs from 0 to 63 over the ZTF focal plane (https://irsa.ipac.caltech.edu/data/ZTF/docs/common/ztf_focal_plane.jpg). In combination with fieldid, this can be used to retrieve additional archive metadata.

Object Right Ascension from the input Reference Image (seed) catalog (https://irsa.ipac.caltech.edu/data/ZTF/docs/releases/dr24/ztf_release_notes_dr24.pdf) corresponding to the fieldID, rcid, and filterid [decimal degrees].

Object Declination from the input Reference Image (seed) catalog (https://irsa.ipac.caltech.edu/data/ZTF/docs/releases/dr24/ztf_release_notes_dr24.pdf) corresponding to the fieldid, rcid, and filterid [decimal degrees].
The number of observation epochs in the lightcurve for this object, included in this data release only.

fields.name: lightcurve
fields.type: struct<hmjd: list<element: double>, mag: list<element: float>, magerr: list<element: float>, clrcoeff: list<element: float>, catflags: list<element: int32>>

metadata.description: Struct holding light curve colummns: hmjd, mag, magerr, clrcoeff, catflags
Partition column. Directory level, equal to 10_000 * floor[Npix / 10_000].

Heliocentric-based Modified Julian Date [days] corresponding to the middle of each exposure and approximate position of the object. The HMJD is derived from "HJD - 2400000.5" where HJD is the Heliocentric Julian Date. HMJD is double precision truncated to 5 decimal places in order to resolve high-cadence observations.

Calibrated magnitude for a source with color g - r = 0 in the AB photometric system. See Cautionary Note #12 in Section 10 (https://irsa.ipac.caltech.edu/data/ZTF/docs/releases/dr24/ztf_release_notes_dr24.pdf).

Corresponding 1-σ uncertainty in mag estimate; excludes the (usually small) uncertainty associated with the calibration zeropoint and possible systematics relative to external photometry catalogs (for example PS1).

Linear color coefficient term from photometric calibration that can be applied to the mag estimate if you know the AB g - r color of your source. See Cautionary Note #12 in Section 10 (https://irsa.ipac.caltech.edu/data/ZTF/docs/releases/dr24/ztf_release_notes_dr24.pdf).

Photometric/image quality flags encoded as bits (Section 9b, https://irsa.ipac.caltech.edu/data/ZTF/docs/releases/dr24/ztf_release_notes_dr24.pdf). In particular, you will always want to exclude observation epochs affected by clouds and/or the moon. These epochs have catflags = 32768 (decimal bit 15).
